title: Beirut tramway and electricity firms merge into one company
why: Private concession utility that supplied Beirut power until the state created EDL in 1954; shows the pre-EDL model.
actors: Société des Tramways et de l'Électricité

title: Taurus Express inaugurated, with service to Tripoli
why: Linked Istanbul, Aleppo and Baghdad with service to Tripoli; discontinued in 1972.

title: Allied engineers finish standard-gauge Haifa–Beirut–Tripoli railway
why: Wartime line, completed by 24 August and extended to Tripoli station by 18 December; Lebanon bought it in 1946.

title: Lebanon buys the Naqoura–Tripoli railway for £5 million
why: The state took over the wartime coastal line that formed the core of its rail network.

title: Abu Ali river flood kills about 160 in Tripoli
why: Torrential storm destroyed bridges, homes and souks and left 2,000 homeless; river later channelled in concrete.

title: Zouk thermal plant starts, first major thermal station
why: Began Lebanon's shift from private concessions and hydropower toward state-run thermal generation near Beirut.

title: Chim earthquake in Chouf kills 136
why: Twin shocks of 5.3 and 5.5 Mw destroyed about 6,000 homes and damaged 17,000, among Lebanon's deadliest modern quakes.

title: Ariana Afghan Airlines Flight 202 crashes near Beirut
why: Airliner crashed near Beirut airport, five years after the airport opened.

title: Beirut port operator renamed Gestion et Exploitation du Port de Beyrouth
why: The French-linked port company became GEPB, which ran the port until its charter expired in 1990.

title: Lebanese railway network reorganised as CEL
why: Source gives 1960 or 1961 for the creation of the state Lebanese Railway body (CEL).

title: Taurus Express service discontinued
why: Ended through rail passenger links from Lebanon to Turkey and Iraq a few years before the war closed the lines.

title: Malév Flight 240 crashes into the sea off Beirut
why: Hungarian airliner crashed near Beirut airport in the first year of the civil war.

title: Beirut–Damascus railway line closed
why: The civil war ended Lebanon's main inland rail link; no regular passenger trains returned.

title: Port of Beirut reopens after nine-month shipping halt
why: Militia clashes had stopped all shipping for nine months in 1976; the port was officially reopened on 15 December.

title: Cabinet decides to build a 500-bed state hospital at Bir Hassan
why: Planned Beirut Governmental Hospital stalled by the civil war and finally opened in 2004 as Rafik Hariri University Hospital.

title: Israeli shelling damages Beirut airport terminal during invasion
why: Terminal damage in 1982; runways were renovated in 1982 and 1984 to keep the airport working through the war.

title: Lebanese Forces militia takes control of Beirut port
why: Militia control of the port lasted until the army pressed it out; the state took direct ownership in 1990.

title: Port of Beirut passes to direct state ownership
why: Charter of the French-linked operator expired; the Lebanese government took over the port at war's end.

title: Dora–Byblos commuter rail service ceases
why: Last passenger commuter service on the Lebanese coastal line ended.

title: Ten-year reconstruction programme for Beirut airport launched
why: Post-war plan that produced the new terminal, completed in stages from 1998 to 2002.

title: Rafik Hariri lays cornerstone of Beirut Governmental Hospital
why: Construction resumed after the war; the hospital was inaugurated on 2 August 2004 at a cost of $121 million.

title: Last regular Lebanese rail operations end
why: Cement trains from Chekka to Beirut stopped; Lebanon has had no regular rail service since.

title: First phase of new Beirut airport terminal completed
why: Gates 1 to 12 opened; a western half followed with gates 13 to 23 inaugurated in 2002.

title: Mudeirej Bridge completed, tallest in Lebanon
why: The 70 m bridge on the Beirut–Damascus road was the highest bridge in the region, and was hit by Israeli air strikes in July 2006.

title: Western terminal of Beirut airport inaugurated
why: Gates 13 to 23 opened, completing the post-war terminal rebuilt in stages from 1998.

title: Beirut Governmental University Hospital inaugurated
why: Largest public hospital in Lebanon, built for $121 million and later named after Rafik Hariri; 25 years from the 1979 decision.

title: Beirut port container terminal subcontracted to BCTC consortium
why: Container operations passed to the Beirut Container Terminal Consortium, which handled the port's boxes until the 2022 CMA CGM contract.

title: Beirut airport renamed after Rafik Hariri
why: The airport took the former prime minister's name in 2005, the year of his assassination.

title: Israeli air force bombs Mudeirej Bridge
why: Strike partly damaged the bridge's base and pillars; USAID-supported reconstruction ($30 million) followed and works finished in 2008.

title: Israel ends air blockade of Lebanon
why: Lifted on 7 September 2006, after the 2006 war and the airport reopening of 17 August.

title: Magnitude 5.1 earthquake hits south Lebanon
why: Ten injured, power cuts and building damage reported; an earthquake swarm affected villages such as Srifa.

title: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 409 crashes off Beirut
why: Aircraft crashed into the Mediterranean shortly after takeoff from Beirut airport on 25 January 2010.

title: Six-storey building collapses in Ashrafieh, Beirut, killing 27
why: Old building housing mostly migrant workers collapsed; many Beirut structures lacked permits, prompting calls for inspections.

title: Powership Orhan Bey arrives in Beirut
why: Second Turkish powership reached Lebanon; connected to the grid near Jiyeh on 3 September 2013.

title: Storm Alexa brings snow and flooding across Lebanon
why: Winter storm of 11-15 December hit more than 800,000 Syrian refugees; eight deaths were attributed to it region-wide.

title: Renovated departures and arrivals terminals open at Beirut airport
why: Upgrade of the terminal built in stages from 1998 to 2002.

title: Lebanon records first COVID-19 death
why: Came three weeks after the first confirmed case of 21 February 2020; a medical emergency was declared on 15 March.

title: Record 2,817 COVID-19 cases reported in one day
why: Peak of the first wave; on 26 December cumulative cases reached 165,933 with 1,000 deaths.

title: Health ministry reserves two million Pfizer-BioNTech doses
why: Lebanon's first vaccine purchase, ahead of the vaccination launch on 14 February 2021.

title: First 50,000 Russian vaccine doses arrive
why: Added a second vaccine source to the national campaign started in February 2021.

title: Armed forces COVID-19 vaccination campaign launched
why: Vaccination extended to army personnel during the third wave.

title: COVID-19 totals near 1.2 million cases and 11,000 deaths
why: Cumulative total as of August 2023, a fatality rate of 0.88 percent.

title: Hariri hospital staff protest at Health Ministry over pay
why: Staff protested for pay and conditions; doctors fell from about 60 to 15 by June 2022.

title: Government orders demolition of Beirut port grain silos
why: Cabinet decision on the damaged silos; the last northern blocks collapsed on 31 July and 4 August 2022.

title: First cholera death in 2022 outbreak
why: Reported days after Lebanon's first case since 1993; 26 cases were confirmed by 12 October.

title: Cholera cases reach 5,105 with 23 deaths
why: Outbreak linked to Syria's cholera crisis; about half of cases were children.

title: Ministry declares cholera outbreak over
why: Closed the 2022-23 outbreak; one study counts 8,072 cases and 23 deaths from October 2022 to June 2023.

title: Second Beirut airport terminal expansion announced
why: Plan announced in March 2023 to extend the terminal.

title: Strike near Rafik Hariri hospital kills 18
why: Unwarned strike near Beirut's main public hospital also injured 60; it came as WHO documented attacks on health care.

title: 226 health workers and patients killed since October 2023
why: Healthcare Attacks Monitoring System count; WHO found 47% of its 137 documented attacks in Lebanon were fatal.

title: World Bank puts war damage at $6.8 billion, needs at $11 billion
why: Assessment covers 8 October 2023 to 20 December 2024; economic losses $7.2 billion; 2024 GDP fell 7.1 percent.

title: Two Tripoli apartment buildings collapse, killing 14
why: Bab al-Tabbaneh collapse after years of neglect; officials had flagged 105 Tripoli buildings for evacuation.

title: Strikes hit Jabal Amel Hospital in Tyre, wounding 86
why: WHO said the emergency and intensive care units were badly damaged; only one of Tyre district's three hospitals stayed fully operational.

title: WHO: 190 attacks on health care killed 128 workers since March
why: Verified over three months of the 2026 war; 332 injured; nearly 3,400 people killed in Lebanon since 2 March.
dup_of: UN and WHO warn strikes on hospitals hit vulnerable patients

title: Tripoli–Homs rail line carries last trains
why: Line damaged in the civil war has not carried trains since 1975; revival attempts in 2001 and 2016 stalled.

title: Lebanon launches tender to study Tripoli–Abboudieh rail section
why: Terms of reference for a feasibility study on the 35 km line; part of a plan to link Tripoli port to Homs.

title: Lebanon and Syria agree joint team to restore Tripoli–Homs rail
why: Ministers met in Damascus and agreed a joint technical team and phased plan; Syria regained World Bank eligibility in 2025.

title: Qlayaat (Rene Mouawad) airport reopens to civilian traffic
why: Salam's flight inaugurated Lebanon's second civilian airport in Akkar; first routes planned to Mersin, Istanbul and Dubai.

title: Lebanese Army takes control of Qlayaat airfield
why: Former Allied and oil-company airstrip became an army base; parliament later met there in 1989 to elect a president.

title: First Iranian fuel tanker docks at Baniyas for Lebanon
why: Hezbollah-arranged shipment announced 19 August 2021, trucked into Lebanon from mid-September amid the fuel crisis.

title: Nasrallah announces Iranian fuel will sail to Lebanon
why: Announced amid queues and blackouts; PM Mikati later called the operation a violation of Lebanese sovereignty.

title: Solar capacity reaches about 1,300 MW by year-end
why: Rooftop and private solar filled the gap left by EDL cuts; capacity was 100 MW in 2020 and 450 MW in 2022.

title: Karpowership stops supplying Lebanon over arrears
why: Power barges halted supply with more than $100 million in unpaid EDL fees; the contract ended in October.
dup_of: Karpowership halts supply over unpaid bills

title: Qaraoun (Naccache) dam completed on the Litani
why: Wikipedia gives 1959 for the 61 m dam, 220 million m3 reservoir; plants followed at 1962 (Abdel Al), 1965 (Arcache), 1968 (Joun).
dup_of: Qaraoun (Naccache) dam completed; Litani scheme built in stages 1962-66

title: Ibrahim Abdel Al hydro plant, 36 MW, starts on Litani
why: First of three plants below Lake Qaraoun; the others followed in 1965 and 1968 to reach 190 MW.

title: Paul Arcache hydro plant, 108 MW, starts on Litani
why: Second Litani plant, the largest, produced with the others about 600 GWh a year.

title: Charles Helou (Joun) hydro plant operational
why: Third Litani plant; the three plants together cover 7 to 10 percent of Lebanon's power needs.

title: Palm Islands declared a protected area by law
why: Three islands off Tripoli became one of Lebanon's first nature reserves; the law number is not given by the page read.

title: Lebanon joins UN climate convention (UNFCCC)
why: Ratified in December 1994; the first national communication followed in 1995, the second in 2011.

title: Lebanon ratifies the Kyoto Protocol
why: Ratified in November 2006, the year of the July war; Lebanon had no binding emissions cap.

title: Committee of Friends of the Cedar Forest founded
why: Environmental NGO active in cedar replanting; SPNL followed in 1986 and the Lebanese Environment Forum in 1994.

title: Society for the Protection of Nature in Lebanon founded
why: SPNL later led the revival of hima community conservation and bird protection.

title: Lebanese Environment Forum formed by eight NGOs
why: Umbrella body that grew to 46 local organisations.

title: Beirut tramway closes in favour of buses and cars
why: Opened in 1908; tracks were removed as cars spread and the system was fully decommissioned in September 1968.

title: Lebanon–Syria Orontes water-sharing agreement
why: Agreement gives Lebanon 80 million m3 a year from the Orontes if flow exceeds 400 million m3.

title: Al-Ghadir wastewater treatment plant completed in Beirut
why: One of the first post-war sewage plants; many later plants were slow to operate.

title: Law 221 reorganises the water sector
why: Merged 22 autonomous water offices into regional water establishments and separated policy from service delivery.

title: Law 241 cuts regional water establishments from five to four
why: Corrected Law 221: Beirut and Mount Lebanon, North, South and Bekaa water establishments.

title: Law 337 adds wastewater treatment to water establishments' duties
why: Extended the regional establishments' remit from supply to sanitation.

title: Israel threatens conflict over Lebanon's Hasbani water diversion
why: Lebanon pumped Hasbani water to supply a village; the dispute showed the cross-border water stakes.

title: Law 401 enables public-private partnerships in water supply
why: Opened the door to private operators; a French firm ran Tripoli's water from 2003 to 2007.

title: Tripoli wastewater treatment plant inaugurated
why: Sidon plant, finished in 2006, became operational in 2010.

title: World Bank approves $200 million for Greater Beirut water supply
why: Funds the Awali–Beirut conveyor from Lake Qaraoun's Awali tunnel; the project took effect in December 2012.

title: Lebanon ratifies WHO tobacco control convention (FCTC)
why: Ratified in 2005; its first tobacco control law, Law 174, came six years later. (OUP paper: signed 2004, ratified 2005; treaty entered into force for Lebanon 7 March 2006)

title: Parliament passes tobacco control Law 174
why: Passed with 126 votes and 2 abstentions; banned indoor smoking and tobacco advertising, though enforcement in venues weakened.

title: Decree sets larger text health warnings on tobacco packs
why: Implemented Law 174's warning rules; warnings later set at 40 percent of the pack surface. (OUP paper: bylaw 8991 of October 2012)

title: Parliament legalises cannabis cultivation for medical and industrial use
why: First Arab country to do so; Law 178 created a licensing authority but did not decriminalise use.

title: Beirut blast damages three hospitals and 12 health centres
why: Capital's hospital capacity fell during the COVID-19 wave; medicine and vaccine stores were destroyed and port supply links cut.

title: Measles outbreak: 519 suspected cases by 28 July
why: Over half were children under five and 77 percent of cases with known status were unvaccinated.

title: Imported polio case reported in north Lebanon
why: A single case from an imported Punjab-strain virus, months after Lebanon's 2002 polio-free certification.

title: Nationwide polio vaccination starts after Syrian cases
why: Campaign covered Lebanese residents and incoming Syrian children at border centres; more rounds followed through 2014.

title: Storm Zina snow and wind kill four refugees, close airport
why: Snow stranded thousands of Syrian refugees in the Bekaa; Beirut airport shut briefly in winds up to 90 km/h.

title: Costa Brava coastal landfill opens near Beirut airport
why: One of the temporary landfills chosen after the 2015 garbage crisis; Bourj Hammoud was the other.

title: Judge orders Costa Brava dump shut over bird-strike risk
why: Mount Lebanon judge Hassan Hamdan acted after a Middle East Airlines plane met birds attracted by the waste near the airport.

title: Algeria offers emergency fuel as Lebanon's reserves run out
why: Followed the nationwide blackout when EDL's fuel stock ran dry in August 2024.

title: Lebanon signs $250 million World Bank loan for power reform
why: First IBRD loan to the sector: national control centre, EDL billing and 150 MW of solar saving about $40 million a year.

title: Energy minister declares unprecedented water shortage
why: Joe Saddi said rainfall was down 51 percent; Lake Qaraoun levels fell 62.5 percent in a year, the worst drought in over 65 years.

title: Lebanon bars Iranian Mahan Air flight from landing in Beirut
why: After an Israeli accusation of cash smuggling; Hezbollah supporters blocked the airport road in protest.

title: Israeli strikes destroy Qasmiyeh Bridge on the coastal highway
why: Last bridge linking the Tyre and Sidon areas across the Litani; destruction isolated the south from the rest of the country.

title: Israel orders destruction of bridges over the Litani
why: Defence minister's order; President Aoun called the first bridge strikes a prelude to a ground invasion.

title: Jiyeh power plant's first two units installed
why: Toshiba units of 65 MW each; Brown Boveri units added in 1980-81 for 346 MW in total.

title: Zouk oil-fired power plant commissioned, 607 MW
why: Four units completed by 1987; the plant later became a major air-pollution source for Zouk Mikael.

title: Northern Coastal Road project signed
why: New 51 km road to link the Beirut–Tripoli highway to the Syrian border; approved on 14 June 2001.

title: Pan-Arab Highway upgrade on Beirut–Damascus road signed
why: Six-lane upgrade from Hazmieh to Saoufar and 36.5 km of new sections to Masnaa; approved 16 April 2003.

title: Tyre Coast Nature Reserve created by Law 708
why: Coast reserve of about 380 ha with Ramsar status from 16 April 1999; a turtle and bird habitat. (Ramsar designation 16 April 1999 per Wikipedia)

title: Environment ministry starts National Reforestation Plan
why: Aimed to lift forest cover to 20 percent over 20 years; the third phase began in 2009.

title: Government launches 40 Million Trees afforestation programme
why: Targets raising forest cover from 13 to 20 percent by 2030.

title: Law 130 adds hima as a fourth protected-area category
why: Community-managed conservation areas gained legal status alongside nature reserves.

title: Wildfires across Lebanon force a national fire strategy
why: More than 200 fires in under 24 hours burned thousands of hectares and exposed weak response capacity.

title: Heavy rain floods Beirut streets and suburbs
why: Ouzai and Jnah were badly hit as roads turned into rivers and drivers were stranded.

title: Storm Hiba covers Lebanon's mountains in snow
why: Snow reached down to 700-900 m; a week-long cold spell hit mountain towns and refugee tents.

title: Turkey–Syria earthquake felt across Lebanon
why: Residents evacuated buildings at about 3:18 am; the interior ministry denied reports of local damage.

title: Lebanon ratifies Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol
why: Commits Lebanon to phase down HFC gases; the Montreal Protocol itself was joined in 1993. (date refined: ratified 5 Feb 2020)

title: Egypt gas supply agreement signed for Deir Ammar via Arab Gas Pipeline
why: Test run began 8 September and regular supplies in October 2009, feeding the Deir Ammar plant near Tripoli.

title: Regular Egyptian gas flows start to Deir Ammar plant
why: First gas-fired supply for Lebanon's grid; interruptions from 2011 meant the link stopped working by the early 2010s.

title: Arab Gas Pipeline interruptions begin to cut Lebanon's gas
why: Sabotage on feeder lines in Sinai disrupted flows; the Lebanese section ceased regular operation by the early 2010s.

title: Peak electricity demand 3,500 MW against 2,200 MW grid capacity
why: The gap pushed households and firms to private diesel generators, which later became a $3 billion parallel system.

title: Parliament passes distributed renewable energy law
why: Law 318 allows net metering and private sales, with systems up to 10 MW; it needs the unformed regulator (ERA) to take effect.

title: Nationwide blackout after EDL runs out of fuel
why: Last working plant stopped over unpaid Iraqi fuel shipments; the airport, water pumps and sewage plants were hit, HRW reported.
dup_of: Nationwide blackout after fuel reserves run out

title: Migrant boat sinks off Tripoli after navy collision, 7 bodies found
why: About 60 aboard; survivors blamed a navy ship, the navy blamed the boat's captain. Dozens stayed missing.

title: Migrant boat from Miniyeh sinks off Tartus, Syria
why: Left on 20 September carrying about 170 people, mostly Syrians; reported tolls range from 94 to about 150.

title: Health ministry launches National Health Strategy: Vision 2030
why: Five pillars including primary care, workforce and digital health, aimed at recovery of a health system hit by the crisis.

title: AUB opens modern 420-bed medical center
why: New AUB Medical Center with outpatient, emergency and research facilities replaced the 1902 hospital.

title: Fuel shortage threatens Lebanese hospitals the day after Tleil blast
why: AUBMC had under 48 hours of fuel for about 150 patients on respirators or dialysis; Hariri hospital ran 2 of 7 generators.

title: Cancer drug shortages and unaffordable treatment reported
why: Hormonal and targeted cancer therapies were scarce; immunotherapies were almost unavailable from July 2021.

title: Volunteers start cleaning Israeli tar spill from Tyre coast reserve
why: About two tonnes of tar hit the Tyre reserve, a turtle nesting site; cleanup was expected to take at least 15 days.

title: Second day of strikes on Jiyeh plant widens oil spill
why: Tanks bombed on 14 and 15 July; 15,000 to 30,000 tonnes of fuel oil fouled 150-170 km of coast; UN put costs at $203 million.
dup_of: Bombing of Jiyeh plant spills about 30,000 t of fuel oil

title: Israeli strike puts main southern electricity substation out of service
why: Part of strikes on power, water and telecom networks in the 2026 war; Bint Jbeil's power station was also damaged.

title: Oxfam: seven water sources damaged in first four days of 2026 war
why: Reservoirs, pipes and pumping stations in Bekaa and Marjayoun were hit; nearly 7,000 people in the Bekaa lost supply.
